sea_lane_graph.creation_method: Manually defined macro navigational waypoint coordinates (57 nodes, 58 edges) calibrated to approximate NGA Pub. 151 corridors for D9.2 algorithm validation and canal bypass testing. NOT programmatically extracted from Eurostat marnet.gpkg.

published_corridor_distances.route: New Orleans, LA (Southwest Pass) to Yokohama, Japan via Panama Canal
published_corridor_distances.substantiation_status: Unverified reconstructed component sum. NGA Pub. 151 does NOT publish a single direct port-to-port table row for New Orleans Southwest Pass fairway to Yokohama. The 9,131 NM, 9,125 NM, and 9,190 NM figures are arithmetic sums reconstructed across intermediate tables whose specific source input distances and matching fairway endpoints are not independently substantiated as a published whole.
published_corridor_distances.discrepancy_explanation: Arithmetic correctness of the component addition (1399 + 50 + 7682 = 9131 vs 1399 + 44 + 7682 = 9125, explaining the 6 NM difference between 50 NM canal fairway transit and 44 NM lock channel) is distinct from verification of the input distances themselves. The input values and fairway endpoints are not independently verified against specific page/table records in NGA Pub. 151.
published_corridor_distances.benchmark_source: USDA AMS AgTransport commercial bulk grain corridor benchmark (USG-JPN-BULK)
published_corridor_distances.distinction_note: The 9,131 NM, 9,125 NM, and 9,190 NM totals are unverified reconstructed component sums, NOT authoritative published fairway distances. Pelagos FreightRoute benchmark (9,150.0 NM) models broader commercial Mississippi River grain elevator loading ranges to Tokyo Bay discharge berths. Computed prototype distance (9,105.57 NM) is the deterministic mathematical output of the 19 calibrated synthetic test waypoints on the prototype graph. It serves as a regression check of pathfinding and geodesic summation, NOT an empirical validation of real-world navigational accuracy.

published_corridor_distances.route: Seattle, WA (Strait of Juan de Fuca) to Yokohama, Japan
published_corridor_distances.unverified_commercial_estimate_note: The previously cited 4,536 NM figure represents an unverified commercial winter route estimate south of the Aleutians; it is NOT an official published table row in NGA Pub. 151. NGA Pub. 151 publishes 4,312 NM (Great Circle) and 4,797 NM (Rhumb line).
published_corridor_distances.endpoint_divergence_note: NGA Pub. 151 published distance (4,312 NM) originates from Seattle inner harbor through Puget Sound. The prototype fixture coordinate for USSEA is at Cape Flattery (48°30'N, 124°45'W), which is 125 NM west of Seattle at the oceanic boundary of the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Because endpoints do not match, published values do not constitute direct validation.
published_corridor_distances.benchmark_source: USDA AMS AgTransport commercial bulk grain corridor benchmark (PNW-JPN-BULK)
published_corridor_distances.distinction_note: Reflects deterministic pathfinding across the 9 prototype test fixture waypoints tracking along 40-48 degrees North latitude. It tests deterministic solver execution, not empirical real-world passage accuracy.

published_corridor_distances.route: Rotterdam, Netherlands to Singapore via Suez Canal
published_corridor_distances.nga_table_reference: Table 1 & Table 2 composite segment sum (Unverified reconstructed reference; NOT an authoritative single-entry published table value)
published_corridor_distances.component_breakdown: Rotterdam (Maas) to Gibraltar (1,845 NM) + Gibraltar to Port Said (1,925 NM) + Suez Canal fairway transit (104 NM) + Suez to Bab-el-Mandeb (1,308 NM) + Bab-el-Mandeb to Singapore Western Fairway (3,106 NM) = 8,288 NM composite sum.
published_corridor_distances.substantiation_status: Unverified composite reference. NGA Pub. 151 publishes inner berth distances (~8,387 NM); the 8,288 NM figure is a reconstructed sum across multiple intermediate junction tables with approximate fairway endpoints, not an independently verifiable direct table row.
published_corridor_distances.distinction_note: Validates multi-chokepoint pathfinding (English Channel, Gibraltar, Suez 104 NM transit, Bab-el-Mandeb, Malacca Strait) on the prototype graph. It verifies algorithm determinism and canal transit inclusion logic, not real-world hydrographic accuracy.

navigational_safety_disclaimer: Coastline boundary checks and sea-lane graph paths reflect macro topological routing only. They do NOT establish that a path is navigationally safe, deep enough for vessel draft, or compliant with international maritime regulations (COLREGS). Pelagos is NOT an ECDIS or passage planning system.
